set.typical_award_size: No fee waiver program exists for affordable multifamily housing. The only adopted County development fee waiver is the ADU and JADU program: a Board resolution of March 11, 2025 extends the Community Development Agency Director's delegated authority to waive or reduce building permit fees through December 31, 2026, up to $1,500 per JADU, $2,500 per ADU, $5,000 for an ADU deed restricted to a moderate-income household (81 to 100 percent AMI) and $10,000 for an ADU deed restricted to a low-income household (up to 80 percent AMI). In 2024 the County processed 27 ADU waivers (one affordable deed-restricted) and 1 JADU waiver totaling $78,000.
set.affordability_requirement: Base ADU and JADU waivers: owner affirms the unit will not be a short-term rental. Higher tiers: recorded deed restriction renting the ADU to a low-income (up to 80 percent AMI) or moderate-income (81 to 100 percent AMI) household.
eligible_project_detail: accessory dwelling units and junior ADUs in unincorporated Marin, with higher waivers for deed-restricted affordable ADUs
set.cycle_notes: Delegated waiver authority runs January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026 (Board action March 11, 2025, extending Resolution 2021-34 and the JADU authority first granted in 2017). Applicants request the waiver with the building permit application to the Building and Safety Division. The General Fund reimburses CDA for non-deed-restricted waivers; the Affordable Housing Fund reimburses waivers for deed-restricted units.
set.next_deadline: Rolling until December 31, 2026, when the current delegation expires unless the Board extends it.
set.prevailing_wage_basis: Waived or reduced fees are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720), but 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential projects built on private property unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment agency or local public housing authority, which typically fits an owner-built ADU. The March 11, 2025 Board letter (https://marin.granicus.com/MetaViewer.php?view_id=33&event_id=3961&meta_id=1365949) states no wage rule. Development Code 22.24.020(C)(2) (https://www.zoneomics.com/code/marin-county-unincorporated-CA/chapter_3) notes that direct financial incentives such as fee waivers may require prevailing wages if State law requires.
set.layering_notes: Corrected from a negative finding: Marin County has an adopted fee waiver, but only for ADUs and JADUs; there is still no countywide fee waiver or reduction for affordable multifamily projects. Development Code 22.24.020(C)(2) says nothing requires direct financial incentives such as fee waivers and leaves them to County discretion, so a multifamily developer would request fee relief case by case (Affordable Housing Fund or a density bonus concession). Separately, the County policies page describes reductions of the affordable housing impact fee or in-lieu fee for projects with affordable units beyond the minimum; that is an inclusionary compliance option under Chapter 22.22 (record 02b451fc33), not a development fee waiver. The ADU waiver stacks with the ADU Center technical assistance pilot.
